claim: As of 2026, Claude paid subscription plans (Pro $20/mo, Max 5x $100/mo, Max 20x $200/mo) include Claude Code access under session-based usage limits, removing the prior restriction that subscriptions only worked in the chat UI.
stance_target: cost structure of agentic coding tool access in 2026
quoted_support: Claude subscriptions now include Claude Code. Paid plans (Pro and Max) unlock the terminal coding agent, so the old "subscriptions only work in the chat UI" rule no longer applies.

claim: For Claude Sonnet 5 API usage, cached input tokens cost $0.20 per 1M tokens versus $3 per 1M for a cache miss, and in agentic coding workflows cache hits typically account for 90-99% of total input tokens because context is re-sent on every turn, making cache-hit rate the dominant cost lever.
stance_target: prompt caching is the primary lever for controlling API cost in agentic coding workloads
quoted_support: Sonnet 5 cached reads cost $0.20 per 1M tokens (Opus $0.50) versus $3/$5 for a cache miss. For agentic coding — where context is re-sent on every turn — cache hits are 90-99% of total input. This is the single biggest lever on API cost.

claim: A typical interactive Claude Code session (~300K input tokens, 15K output tokens) at an 80% cache-hit rate costs approximately $0.45 on official Sonnet 5 API rates, dropping to approximately $0.29 at a >99% cache-hit rate achievable via a dedicated caching gateway.
stance_target: per-session cost modeling for agentic coding API usage
scope_conditions: modeled Claude Code session, Sonnet 5 pricing, 2026 (vendor-produced estimate from TeamoRouter, a caching-gateway seller — note commercial interest)
quoted_support: Total per session ≈ $0.45 ... Total per session ≈ $0.29 (vs $0.45 official)

claim: Subscription pricing is cheaper for light-to-moderate interactive Claude use (roughly under 5-10 sessions/day), while API pay-per-use becomes cheaper the moment usage is automated (CI/CD, background agents), spiky/unbounded, or spread across a team, because subscriptions impose session and weekly usage caps.
stance_target: autonomous/automated agent workloads are economically forced onto metered API billing rather than flat subscriptions
quoted_support: subscriptions are cheaper for interactive humans within their session limits, and API is cheaper the moment you exceed those limits or add automation.

claim: Anthropic's batch API roughly halves prices for non-urgent jobs, making it the cheapest API option for time-insensitive workloads.
stance_target: cost optimization options for non-time-sensitive agent workloads
quoted_support: Anthropic's batch API roughly halves prices for non-urgent jobs. If your workload is not time-sensitive, batch is the cheapest possible API option.
